nodes.summary: For $k \ge 0$ let $T_k = k(k+1)/2$ be the $k$-th triangular number. For every natural number $j$, the number of ordered quadruples $(k_1, k_2, k_3, k_4)$ of integers with $0 \le k_i \le j$ and $T_{k_1} + T_{k_2} + T_{k_3} + T_{k_4} = j$ equals $\sigma(2j+1)$, the sum of the positive divisors of $2j+1$.
nodes.title: Legendre's four-triangular-numbers theorem

nodes.summary: For every integer $k \ge 1$ there is a natural number $g$ such that every natural number $n$ is a sum of $g$ $k$-th powers of natural numbers, that is, $n = x_1^k + \dots + x_g^k$ for some $x_1, \dots, x_g \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Hilbert–Waring theorem

nodes.summary: Call a rational quaternion a Hurwitz integer if its four coordinates are either all integers or all of the form $a + \tfrac12$ with $a$ an integer. For every positive integer $\ell$ with $\ell \equiv 1$ or $\ell \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ there is a natural number $g$ such that every Hurwitz integer is a sum of at most $g$ $\ell$-th powers of Hurwitz integers.
nodes.title: Waring's problem for Hurwitz quaternion integers
